notes:
Initial qualification for Private VPC deployment. GrayHaven (FS analytics) has strict data residency and key management requirements — all model inputs that contain account identifiers/transactional PII must remain in customer-controlled AWS accounts and never traverse public internet. Customer expects customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS CMK or HSM-backed) with annual rotation and key access audit. They require CloudTrail-grade audit logging for all control-plane actions and token-level access logs for inference requests (30+ day retention to start).

Architecture constraints discussed: must live in their AWS org (landing in eu-west-1 primary, na-east-1 secondary for failover). No public IPs on inference workers; inbound only from internal app subnets via VPC peering or Transit Gateway. Outbound egress must go through corporate egress proxy; explicit allow list for Redwood control-plane endpoints or use PrivateLink endpoints. Preferred topology: private subnets for GPU worker fleet, NAT/egress via centrally managed NAT gateways, S3 and ECR access via VPC endpoints, and optional AWS PrivateLink to Redwood control-plane for metrics/rollouts.

POC ask: 6-week POC to validate: (1) VPC topology and PrivateLink connectivity, (2) KMS integration with CMK for model weights and logs, (3) audit log export to their SIEM, (4) throughput/latency validation for chat path with 40ms token latency target p50 and sustained 100 qps for embeddings rerank. They will run a small synthetic workload (mixed chat + long-doc embeddings).

Security review status: customer provided security questionnaire on 2026-03-02 (answers due from Redwood by 2026-03-12). SE walked through the tricky items: key escrow (customer insists no escrow), retention policy for logs, and requirement for SOC2 + ISO27001 evidence. Legal team flagged indemnity clause in standard T&Cs; procurement engaged.

Quotes/notes from stakeholders: "We cannot allow any inference payloads to be processed outside our VPC" — VP Engineering. "Need CMK, or we won't move forward" — Security Lead.

Next steps (short): deliver a VPC sketch+traffic flow diagram, confirm PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway tradeoffs, provide example IAM roles/policies and KMS integration steps, supply SOC2 artifacts and signature on DPA draft. SE to coordinate with Solutions Eng for demo environment.

Risks: cross-region replication requirements could add latency and cost; Customer-managed keys require clear key policy docs; outbound firewall rules in their environment may block Redwood endpoints — need list of IPs/FQDNs or PrivateLink plan.
